topics.title: Sanctioned housing is not the same as housing delivered.
topics.deck: Read the administrative stages before attributing a housing figure to displaced families.
topics.scope: Manipur statewide PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0; not an IDP-only series
findings: The ministry reports 56,045 sanctioned houses, 49,846 grounded and 20,591 completed or delivered. These are statewide programme totals, not a count of houses delivered to displaced families.
The reply reports ₹867.95 crore central assistance involved, ₹582.36 crore released and ₹468.53 crore utilised. It does not provide the requested IDP-specific district/site breakdown.
limits: Sanction, grounding and completion are different administrative stages; these aggregate stocks do not establish cohort-level delay or construction quality.
Urban housing figures cannot be relabelled as rural, all-housing or IDP-specific delivery.
questions: How many verified IDP households received completed houses, by site and completion date?
Which sanctions, releases and utilisation certificates relate to those same households and projects?
Are completed homes occupied, habitable and connected to water, electricity, schools and transport?

topics.title: An allocation is not proof of a household receipt.
topics.deck: Relief-camp supply needs a consistent period, beneficiary denominator and delivery trail.
topics.reference: Reply 20 August 2025; cumulative distribution period unspecified
topics.scope: Rice assistance and relief-camp distribution in Manipur
findings: The reply records rice allocations of 30,000 MT in May 2023 and 1,085.36 MT in September 2024 for specified non-NFSA assistance periods.
It separately reports, on information from the State, 24,174.90 MT distributed through Deputy Commissioners to relief camps. The distribution period and a camp-wise breakdown are not provided.
limits: The allocations and distribution figure have different or unstated periods. A distribution-to-allocation percentage would mix denominators.
Reported distribution is not independently audited household receipt, nutritional adequacy or regularity.
questions: What are camp-wise opening stocks, receipts, distributions and closing stocks for the same month?
How many residents were served, and how were changes in camp population recorded?
What shortages were reported, investigated and resolved, with dates?

topics.title: Follow the rehabilitation provision into verified delivery.
topics.deck: The 2026–27 budget identifies a commitment; outcomes require a separate evidence chain.
topics.scope: Statewide IDP rehabilitation and resettlement budget provision
findings: The budget speech provides ₹734 crore for IDP rehabilitation and resettlement in 2026–27. This is a budget provision, not expenditure or a verified count of resettled households.
limits: The speech amount is not allocated to individual Assembly constituencies in this dataset.
Sanctions, releases, expenditure, compensation receipts and safe sustained resettlement are different measures.
questions: Which schemes and budget heads compose the provision, and what has been released against each?
What household-level receipt and independent completion evidence supports reported resettlement?
Do outcome reports distinguish return, relocation, temporary shelter and safe sustained occupancy?

topics.title: A road provision does not establish a working route.
topics.deck: Measure accessibility and completion separately from money announced.
topics.scope: Statewide road provision; additional funding streams identified separately in the speech
findings: The budget speech provides ₹914 crore for roads in BE 2026–27 and identifies supplementary funding channels. A provision alone does not establish road completion, maintenance quality or reliable travel.
limits: No constituency allocation or currently passable road length is inferred from this statewide figure.
Funding streams need project-level reconciliation before aggregation to avoid double-counting.
questions: Which road packages have work orders, deadlines, payments and independently verified milestones?
How many days were critical routes fully usable, and what caused interruptions?
Are maintenance obligations, defect correction and safety inspection records published?

topics.title: Connections measure infrastructure, not continuous service.
topics.deck: AMRUT figures need their programme scope and service limits attached.
topics.reference: Lok Sabha reply 2 April 2026 · annexure reporting date not separately specified
topics.scope: Manipur state row for AMRUT, AMRUT 2.0 and convergence, as reported by States/UTs
findings: The annexure reports 28,947 households covered with new or serviced tap connections and 4,000 with sewer connections or septage management. It combines programme and convergence reporting.
limits: New and serviced connections are combined; these are not necessarily all new physical connections.
These figures do not establish hours of supply, water quality, affordability or rural coverage.
questions: Which urban bodies and projects contribute the reported households, and how is duplication prevented?
What proportion receive prescribed quantity and quality regularly?
Which sewage or septage assets are operating, and where are monitoring results available?

topics.title: A reform agreement is a starting point for service evidence.
topics.deck: Track the 2026 agreement without presenting its objectives as achieved coverage.
topics.scope: Manipur agreement under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0; rural water governance
findings: The Ministry of Jal Shakti reports signing a reform-linked MoU with Manipur on 10 June 2026. The stated model emphasises local participation and accountable rural water service.
limits: An MoU confirms an institutional action, not functional household coverage or successful delivery.
No statewide rural service percentage or constituency-specific estimate is derived from this release.
questions: What service-level targets, baselines, implementation dates and responsibilities were agreed?
Which systems have verified functionality, quality tests and funded maintenance?
How are community monitoring results and complaints independently checked?

topics.title: Higher utilisation than releases needs an opening-balance check.
topics.deck: A funding comparison can mislead when expenditure draws on earlier balances.
topics.reference: Written-reply release 28 July 2026 · last five years and current year, cumulative
findings: The primary release reports ₹21.37 crore released and ₹52.17 crore utilised for Manipur. Its footnote says many States held opening SNA balances on 1 April 2021.
The comparison is therefore not treated as overspending or an invalid total. A closed fund-flow identity requires opening balances and the same accounting scope.
limits: The national training and placement totals in the release are not Manipur outcomes.
Funds utilised do not measure local employment, retained jobs, earnings or training quality. An expenditure/release efficiency percentage is withheld.
questions: What opening balance, State share and other adjustments reconcile the same-period accounts?
How many Manipur trainees completed training, entered jobs and remained employed at six and twelve months?
Are wages, employer verification, dropout and grievance outcomes reported by cohort and district?
